questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Suriname?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: Paramaribo is the capital city, in which resides almost half of the country's population.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Suriname?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Suriname on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: There are border disputes with French Guiana and Guyana all to the south of the country.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Suriname?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: The official name of the country is Republiek Suriname (this is Dutch and translates to Republic of Suriname).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Before that, it was a part of the Kingdom of the _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: Before that, it was a part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “After the second Anglo-Dutch War England traded any claims to the territory for New _____ which became New York.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “became”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Suriname article.

questions.proof: After the second Anglo-Dutch War England traded any claims to the territory for New Amsterdam which became New York.
